verses.sa: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च श्रृणुयादपि यो नरः । सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
verses.tr: Even a person who listens to this with trust and without fault-finding becomes free and reaches the auspicious realms earned by noble action.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna finishes his teaching and opens the door to liberation beyond Arjuna. Listen to who else can enter.

body.text: Even a person who listens to this with trust and without fault-finding becomes free and reaches the auspicious realms earned by noble action. Listen to the word anasyuh, without fault-finding. The teaching does not demand a scholar, only a listener who comes without mockery to hear what is said. Krishna asks Arjuna directly if his confusion is gone, closing the conversation he began.

verses.sa: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा । कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥
verses.tr: O Partha, have you heard this with one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed in you?
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has finished his long teaching and turns to Arjuna, checking whether the words have landed. The war still waits, but the real test is whether Arjuna's ignorance and confusion have been broken.

body.text: O Partha, have you heard this with one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed in you? Krishna asks two questions, one about listening and one about being free. The word krsna uses for listening, srutam, is just the past tense of hearing, and he asks if Arjuna heard this with ekagrena cetasa, a mind gathered into a single point. Arjuna answers that his delusion is gone and he will do as Krsna says.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत । स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: By your grace, O Achyuta, my delusion is destroyed and memory restored. I stand free of doubt and will do what you say.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: In the final verse of the Gita, Arjuna answers Krishna. What has changed inside him? Listen for the word that tells you.

body.text: Arjuna says: By your grace, O Achyuta, my delusion is destroyed and memory restored. I stand free of doubt and will do what you say. Arjuna names one thing he has received, smriti, memory. Krishna's teaching has brought it back, and with it the confusion that clouded his sight. Sanjaya closes the Gita by calling this dialogue wondrous and hair-raising.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः । संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Thus I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha.
verses.angle: Partha, the great-souled one, has returned to clarity
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya has watched the whole war. Now he tells Dhritarashtra what he heard. Listen to how he describes the talk between Krishna and Arjuna.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Thus I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha. Sanjaya names the two speakers as Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha. The word mahatmanah, great-souled, sits right beside Partha, marking that Arjuna has come out of his grief and into his true self. He closes by saying this same conversation was a supreme secret that he heard directly from the Lord of yoga himself.

verses.tr: By Vyasa's grace, I heard this supreme secret yoga directly from Krishna, the Lord of yoga, as he spoke it himself.
verses.angle: Saakshat, directly, the source of the teaching
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya now names the exact source of the teaching, and points to one word that seals its origin. Listen for it.

body.text: By Vyasa's grace, I heard this supreme secret yoga directly from Krishna, the Lord of yoga, as he spoke it himself. The word is saakshat, directly. Sanjaya did not read a text; he heard this supreme secret spoken live by Krishna himself, a direct transmission from the Lord of yoga. Remembering this direct teaching, Sanjaya rejoices again and again, carrying the dialogue forward.

verses.sa: राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् । केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
verses.tr: O King, remembering again and again this wondrous, holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya finishes by telling the king that he does not merely report the Gita, but lives inside it. Listen to how he describes his own response.

body.text: O King, remembering again and again this wondrous, holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again. Sanjaya calls the conversation between Krishna and Arjuna wonderful and holy, and he says he rejoices again and again every time he remembers it. He remembers the form of Krishna and feels wonder and joy again and again.

verses.sa: तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः । विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
verses.tr: Remembering that astonishing form of Krishna again and again, I feel great wonder, O King, and I rejoice again and again.
verses.angle: Repeated remembering keeps the vision alive
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: In the last verse, Sanjaya said he rejoiced at the holy dialogue. Now he returns to the vision that started it all.

body.text: Remembering that astonishing form of Krishna again and again, I feel great wonder, O King, and I rejoice again and again. Recalling Krishna's cosmic form again and again, Sanjaya feels great wonder and keeps rejoicing. The vision of Krishna and Arjuna together is the source of all prosperity and victory, says Sanjaya.

verses.sa: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
verses.tr: Where Krishna, the master of yoga, is present, and where Arjuna, the bow-bearer, is present, there are prosperity, victory, glory, and firm justice. This is my conviction.
verses.angle: Right action carries its own victory.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

body.text: Where Krishna, the master of yoga, is present, and where Arjuna, the bow-bearer, is present, there are prosperity, victory, glory, and firm justice. This is my conviction. Sanjaya's closing verdict: where Krishna and Arjuna stand together, prosperity, victory, glory and justice follow. Here the Gita comes to rest.
